key_insight: Foundation interatomic potentials capture disorder in Cu–Zr–Al metallic glasses most reliably when their pre-training includes liquid and amorphous structures.
engineering_relevance: Broadly pre-trained potentials can reduce reliance on composition-specific models for simulating metallic-glass structure and properties, provided their dynamics are carefully validated.
method: Benchmark MACE foundation models against EAM during molecular-dynamics quenches.
Validate at Cu46Zr46Al8 and across the ternary’s good glass-forming region using DFT and experiment.
Test fine-tuning on surrogate-generated glass structures and ASSYST-generated small periodic cells.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that OMAT-pre-trained models outperform composition-specific EAM, glass-focused fine-tuning yields modest gains, and small-crystalline-cell specialization degrades disorder modeling.
watch_item: Results concern Cu–Zr–Al glasses; transfer to other alloy systems requires validation rather than assuming universal accuracy.
paper_title: Foundation interatomic potentials capture structural disorder in metallic glasses
